title: Split cli.py and ops.py
lead: `cli.py` is split into a parser table and handlers per command group, and `ops.py`'s read-only queries move out of the mutation module, with no change in behaviour, output bytes or error codes.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** any behaviour, output or error-code change; lazy subparsers; renaming commands.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `src/slicer/cli.py` is 5,180 lines; its `build_parser` is 946 lines (`cli.py:4034-4979`), the largest unit in the codebase. `src/slicer/ops.py` is 4,015 lines and is meant to be the single mutation path (AGENTS.md), but it also holds ranking and reporting queries such as `_ranked_pool` (138 lines) and `outline_report` (121 lines). Nearly every slice touches one of the two, so their size raises review cost for every relay and the chance of merge conflicts between slices run in parallel. Found by the Go rewrite evaluation (`research/go-rewrite-evaluation.md`); figures re-measured on main at a96b7e8 on 2026-11-02, when the architect's design round for this slice ran.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
Owner-approved design (2026-11-02): flat modules beside `cli.py`; `cli.py` stays the entry point (`pyproject.toml` and `__main__.py` unchanged) and keeps `main`, `_parser` and `_cached_parser`.

- `src/slicer/cli.py` (about 190 lines after the split): `main`, `_recursive`, `_error_envelope`, `_fail`, `_parser`, `_cached_parser`, `_warn_code_mismatch`, `_changes_state`. It imports `build_parser` by name from `cli_parser`.
- New `src/slicer/cli_common.py` (about 660 lines): exit codes, shared flags, `_emit` and the output helpers, `_mutating` and its helpers, `_state`, the check helpers `_post_check` and friends, `_ParserError`, `_ArgumentParser`, and the other helpers every handler module shares. It imports no `cli*` module at load time; one lazy helper returns `cli._cached_parser()`.
- New handler modules, each importing only `cli_common`: `cli_ai.py` (AI onboarding, about 380 lines), `cli_relay.py` (relay-roles and relay-run, about 400), `cli_setup.py` (init, setup-git, merge drivers, about 170), `cli_prose.py` (prose, template, config, sections, goals, catalog, about 400), `cli_track.py` (tracking writes, about 760), `cli_queue.py` (tracking reads: next, plan-parallel, list, find, deps, show, status, about 960), `cli_report.py` (render, sync, verify, refs, check, stats, snapshot, log, tui, about 250).
- New `src/slicer/cli_parser.py` (about 950 lines): `build_parser` moved verbatim, then split into contiguous section functions called in today's order (the `add_parser` order drives the help listing) in a separate commit.
- `src/slicer/ops.py` and new `src/slicer/queries.py` (about 630 lines): the read-only ranking and reporting functions move to `queries.py` (`_ranked_pool`, `next_item`, `next_batch`, `plan_parallel`, `held_flags`, the path and readiness helpers, `custom_queue`, `actor`, `slivers_of`, `dependents`, `_blockers`, `_reclaim_check`, `remove_preview` and their result types). `outline_report` and its validators stay in `ops.py`. Callers import from `queries`; there is no re-export. `queries.py` imports only `graph`, `ids`, `paths`, `vcs`, `model`, `config`, `errors`, and `State` under `TYPE_CHECKING`.
- Callers and tests: `snapshot.py`, `tui.py` (`_heal_render`), the `ops.py` docstring near line 1390, and the test files that patch moved names (dotted patch strings such as `slicer.cli.store.*` retarget to the real module; `_via_editor`, `_heal_render`, `_read_user_file`, `datetime`, `_ai_project`). A patched helper called from another module is called module-qualified so one lookup site exists per name.
- Docs: `ARCHITECTURE.md` (module map, diagram, the cycle paragraph, "A new command belongs in `ops.py`"), `AGENTS.md` ("never straight into `cli.py`"), `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- `tests/affected.py` refuses Python files under `src/` its map does not name, so every step runs the full discover instead of `affected.py --run`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - None new by design: the full suite, `slicer check` and byte-identical `render` output are the safety net. Add `test_Ops_QueryModule_WritesNothing` if the architect wants the read-only split enforced (the query module imports no writer).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. An architect proposes the module boundaries and the order of moves; the owner approves them.
2. Move code in small steps, each green on the full suite, preferably at a quiet point in the queue so parallel slices do not conflict.
3. Update `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3.12 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` passes.
- `slicer check` passes; `render` output is byte-identical before and after.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit per move on the slice branch, or one commit if the owner prefers; the owner lands it.
